Cover. Under Pressure Rating: a reproducible pressure-performance rating for the SupeRR Selector brief, built for Rajasthan Royals.

Problem: who is reliable under pressure?

The brief: identify the most reliable players under pressure (top 10 batters, top 10 bowlers) using the ball-by-ball data, compare them with their usual level, explain the method, and show how they could strengthen Rajasthan Royals for the IPL 2027 auction.
DEFINE PRESSURE
KEY PROBLEMS
  • "Pressure" has no agreed definition
  • Death overs ≠ always pressure
NEEDS
  • A measurable, match-aware definition
  • Proof it captures decisive moments
MEASURE FAIRLY
KEY PROBLEMS
  • Openers and finishers face different balls
  • A run is worth more in a tight chase
NEEDS
  • Compare each ball with an average player in the same spot
  • Charge wickets by their real cost
VS USUAL LEVEL
KEY PROBLEMS
  • Good players look good everywhere
  • Pressure skill vs overall skill
NEEDS
  • Score pressure level minus own usual level
  • Report both side by side
SMALL SAMPLES
KEY PROBLEMS
  • Most players have < 300 pressure balls
  • One hot week tops a raw table
NEEDS
  • Shrink noisy estimates toward the mean
  • Minimum sample rules
PROVE IT WORKS
KEY PROBLEMS
  • Any formula can be tuned to look right
  • No ground truth for "clutch"
NEEDS
  • Test on matches the method never saw
  • Rule fixed before seeing results
BUILD FOR RR
KEY PROBLEMS
  • A ranking is not a squad plan
  • Most stars are under contract
NEEDS
  • Find RR's pressure gaps
  • Match players to gaps and availability
WHY RAW NUMBERS MISLEAD
Six, last over of a chaseNeed 1 off 3; win probability 79% → 100%
Six, 10th over, 80 runs aheadWin probability hardly moves
Raw statsBoth = 6 runs, same strike-rate boost
Our rating: high-pressure ballCounted in the pressure sample, valued vs an average player in that exact state
Our rating: routine ballCounts toward the player's usual level, not pressure

Top 10 batters + top 10 bowlers
ranked by a rating chosen on unseen matches
An IPL 2027 plan for RR
pressure gaps by phase, player fit, availability
Interactive dashboard
every number checked against the pipeline (10,172 checks)

raw CSVs → final lists → report, seed 42

Concept 1: measuring pressure

A real chase: Kolkata Knight Riders vs Rajasthan Royals, IPL 2026
Target 156. Line = win probability of the chasing side before each ball. Bars = Pressure Index; pink = top 30% of all balls (our "under pressure").
PRESSURE INDEX IN PLAIN WORDS
1 · Game stateruns needed, balls & wickets left, phase, target, Elo gap
2 · Win probabilityLightGBM model: chance the batting side wins from here
3 · Leveragefor every possible next ball (dot, 1, 2, 4, 6, wicket, extra): how far would win probability move? Weighted average of those swings.
4 · Pressure Indexleverage (average ball = 1) × 1.15 in knock-outs
Top 30% = under pressurecut-off PI ≥ 1.11
Is the win-probability model any good?
Out-of-fold predictions, calibration (predicted vs actual win rate)
0.896
AUC, chasing innings
0.706
AUC, first innings (harder: no target yet)
Monotone constraints (more runs needed never helps the batting side), DLS-revised targets, 5 folds grouped by match.
How to read the chart
  • Early balls barely move the result → low Pressure Index, not counted as pressure.
  • As the chase tightens, every ball can swing it → bars turn pink. The last over carries the most pressure of the match.
  • Pressure follows the match situation, not the over number: a collapse in over 8 can be pressure; a cruise in over 19 is not.
  • Why 30%? reliable ratings while keeping enough players eligible (next slide).
PROBLEMDATA & PRESSUREMETHODITERATIONSRESULTSRR STRATEGYREPRODUCE05
Pressure = how much the next ball can change who wins. Computed from a win-probability model, averaged over every possible outcome of the next ball.

Concept 1b: is that the right definition?

Does our definition find the decisive balls?
Share of all match-deciding win-probability swing that lands in the flagged balls, and the ratio to their share of balls
Why the top 30%?
Split-half reliability of player ratings (does a player's score on half the matches predict the other half?) and players left eligible, per cut-off
Where pressure lives (chasing innings)
Average Pressure Index by over and wickets lost. Darker pink = more pressure.
WHAT THE CHECKS SHOWED
  • Leverage puts 2.06× its share of match-deciding swing into flagged balls; rule-based definitions only ~1.2–1.3×.
  • Pressure is spread over the innings: 35% of pressure balls are in the powerplay, 41% in the middle overs, 23% at the death.
  • Reliability is a plateau (ρ ≈ 0.23–0.33) from top 40% to top 15%. Top 30% sits on it and keeps ~150 players per role eligible; top 15% would leave ~90.
  • Wickets in hand matter: 4 down in over 15 of a chase is far more pressure than 1 down.
Where the pressure balls fall (all 58,197 flagged balls)
Powerplay 35%
Middle overs 41%
Death 23%

Three definitions were tested. The model-based leverage concentrates twice its share of the decisive swing into the flagged balls.

Concept 2: context-adjusted value

CONCEPT 2 · VALUE OF A BALL, WORKED ON A REAL DELIVERY
The situationRinku Singh on strike vs Brijesh Sharma. Need 1 off 3, 4 wickets left.
Average player hereModel trained on all other matches: expected runs 1.91, chance of getting out 12.7%
What happenedHit for 6, not out. Win probability 79% → 100%.
Value = (runs − expected runs) − wicket cost × (out − chance of out)= (6 − 1.91) − 1.51 × (0 − 0.127) = +4.28 runs for the batter, -4.25 for the bowler
What a wicket costs
Runs the batting side loses on average when a wicket falls (from an expected-remaining-runs model)
Bowlers get the mirror image
value = (expected runs conceded − runs conceded) + wicket cost × (wicket − chance of a wicket). The same six above is -4.25 for Brijesh Sharma.
WHY THIS IS FAIR
Same yardstick for every role
an opener is compared with average openers' outcomes in powerplay states; a finisher with death-over states
Wickets are not free
losing a wicket early costs ~9.6 runs; at the death ~2.6. A batter who slogs and gets out pays for it
Opposition counts
Elo in the win-probability model; balls against Associates weighted 0.5
Competition-aware
IPL and T20I balls compared within their own competition, pace vs spin separated
WHAT WE ADD UP PER PLAYER
MeasureMeaning
Pressure value /100runs above an average player per 100 pressure balls
Usual value /100same thing on all other balls
Upliftpressure minus usual: does he rise or dip?
Consistencyshare of pressure matches with a top-quartile contribution
Pressure SR / economysolution B's rate measures on the highest-leverage balls
PROBLEMDATA & PRESSUREMETHODITERATIONSRESULTSRR STRATEGYREPRODUCE07
Each ball is compared with what an average player would produce in the identical situation, with wickets charged at their real cost.

Concepts 3 & 4: small samples and certainty

Concept 3: shrinkage (empirical Bayes)
Each batter's raw pressure value (grey) and the shrunk estimate we use (pink). Small samples move most toward the average.
THE IDEA IN ONE PICTURE
New restaurant2 reviews, both 5★
Established restaurant800 reviews, average 4.6★
Which is safer?2 reviews could be luck. We pull small samples toward the average until they earn trust.
  • Estimate how much players really differ vs how noisy each player's average is.
  • Weight = how much to trust the player's own number. More balls → more trust.
  • Runs and wickets are shrunk separately (a single dismissal is worth ~9 runs and swamps everything else).
  • Final rating = 50/50 blend of the direct estimate and a hierarchical one (own overall level + shrunk pressure difference).
CONCEPT 4 · HOW SURE ARE WE? (BOOTSTRAP)
837 matchesthe real history
Resample 300×draw matches with replacement: some appear twice, some not at all
Re-rate every timesame recipe, new sample → new top 10
P(top 10)share of the 300 runs where the player stays in the top 10
+ robustness checksre-rank under 12 (bat) / 39 (bowl) alternative specs: IPL-only, T20I-only, other thresholds, near-best methods
PROBLEMDATA & PRESSUREMETHODITERATIONSRESULTSRR STRATEGYREPRODUCE08
Shrinkage stops a player with a lucky handful of balls from topping the list. The bootstrap tells us how stable each rank is.

How we refined it: 12 steps, each tested

0 · Simplest ideasDROPPED
rank by raw pressure SR / economy or most pressure balls→ volume ≈ random; finishers dominate
1 · Define pressureKEPT
rules vs stress score vs model leverage→ leverage 2× decisive share → adopted
2 · A v1DROPPED
runs above expected, one joint shrinkage→ reliability 0.01 / 0.07: one dismissal swamps signal
3 · A v2STEP
shrink runs and wickets separately→ small gain (0.04 / 0.05)
4 · A v3DROPPED
win-probability lens (WPA/LI)→ looked great (0.31 / 0.23) but measured context, not skill
5 · A v4STEP
centre WPA/LI within innings × phase→ honest but modest (0.11 / 0.13)
6 · A v5STEP
run value + direct shrinkage→ most faithful, least stable
7 · A v6KEPT
blend direct + hierarchical, usual level, consistency→ 0.22 / 0.17; predicts 2025–26 from 2022–24
8 · Solution BKEPT
independent: pressure SR, economy + WPA→ strong on strike rate, ignores dismissals
9 · A vs BSTEP
same unseen splits, 8 targets→ no overall winner: each found something
10 · Hybrid tournamentKEPT
60+ blends, 3 pools, gates, extra terms→ beats both parents on worst case
11 · Brief constraintKEPT
must score pressure vs usual level→ bowler score gains uplift term
Reliability pairs = split-half ρ for batters / bowlers. KEPT STEP DROPPED

Choosing the method: a held-out tournament

837 matches
30 random half-splits
6 past → future cutstrain on first 50–85% by date
60+ candidates per roleA, B, blends (weights 0.33–1.0), 3 pool rules, ± usual-level & consistency terms, ± gate, simple baselines
8 targets × 2 schemes = 16 cellsbatters: strike rate, runs above expected, win prob. added, dismissal avoidance · bowlers: economy, runs saved, win prob. added, wickets — each under both pressure definitions, measured only on unseen matches
Gain(mean target of the picked 10 − pool mean) ÷ pool SD
Rule fixed in advancemust include pressure-vs-usual; best worst cell, then best mean within 0.03

The final recipes

BATTER SCORE
Final batter scorez-scored, higher = better
A compositecontext-adjusted, shrunk
B strike-rate ensembleno shrinkage
Pressure rating × 0.51runs above expected, 50/50 direct + hierarchical
Uplift × 0.15pressure level − own usual level
Consistency × 0.34share of pressure matches with a top-quartile contribution
SR at leverage pct 75+top quarter of balls in each innings
SR at leverage pct 85+top 15%
BOWLER SCORE
Final bowler scorez-scored, higher = better
Rating blend0.2 × A rating + 0.8 × B economy + WPA
Upliftpressure − own usual level (the brief)
A pressure rating × 0.2runs saved vs expected, shrunk
B economy runs per ball at leverage pct 70+, shrunk (k = 500)
B win prob. added per ball at pct 70+, shrunk; with economy = B (× 0.8)
Delivered gatea bowler whose observed pressure value is below league average cannot rank above one who delivered
SAME FOR BOTH
  • Pool: ≥150 pressure balls, ≥12 matches, ≥150 usual balls (won the pool test).
  • IPL + T20I; Associates weighted 0.5; Elo inside the win-probability model.
  • Weights in A's composite ∝ each part's split-half reliability; uplift floored at 0.15.
  • Every number on these trees was chosen by the tournament, not by hand.

How sure are we?

Batters
P(top 10) across 300 resamples · right: specs agreeing
Bowlers
P(top 10) across 300 resamples · right: specs agreeing
HOW TO READ THIS
  • Ranks 1–4 in each list are well supported: high P(top 10) and most specifications agree.
  • Ranks 7–10 sit in a crowded band: the next 5–10 players are close.
  • No method keeps more than ~6–7 of its 10 names across resamples. That is a limit of the data, not of one method.
  • Hazlewood is top 10 in 39 of 39 specifications; Abhishek Sharma in 12 of 12.
LIMITS WE STATE OPENLY
Modest predictive power
+0.3 to +0.45 pool SD on unseen matches; wicket/dismissal targets are the noisiest
First innings is harder
AUC 0.71: no target yet, so first-innings leverage is flatter
Missing extras
runs beyond the first on wides/byes/leg-byes absent; chases ~1 run short
Cross-competition mix
players whose pressure balls are mostly T20I (or mostly IPL) carry extra uncertainty

Annexure A · How we analysed the data

First innings
Average Pressure Index by over × wickets lost
Chasing innings
Average Pressure Index by over × wickets lost
How pressure is distributed
All 193,988 balls by Pressure Index (pink = top 30%)
WHAT THE EXPLORATION TOLD US
1
Pressure balls are not slower
run rate 9.12 under pressure vs 8.63 routine; boundaries 19.7% vs 18.2%
2
…but mistakes cost more
dismissal 5.77% vs 5.46% per ball, and each wicket swings the result further
3
Chases carry the sharpest pressure
the second innings has a target, so every ball's swing is larger (AUC 0.896 vs 0.706)
4
Wickets in hand drive it
the same over is far more pressured 4–5 down than 0–1 down (heatmaps)

THE HONEST CASE
  • Middle overs 278 balls (+36.7/100) and death 126 balls (+32.5): exactly where RR rank 7th and 5th.
  • Chasing (+38.0/100) and setting (+32.6): delivers in both.
  • 2025 was quiet (+2.4/100); 2026 back to +40.2.
  • He gets out more often under pressure (every 16.5 balls vs 29.5): the price of attacking, already charged in his +35.5 value.
  • Overseas slot and an SRH contract: route is a trade (to 9 Dec) or a release. Fallback: Dewald Brevis.

Annexure C · War-room moments

The result that looked too goodSolution A v3 jumped to 0.31 reliability. A diagnostic showed it was measuring match context, not skill.→ Dropped it, even though it flattered us.
Two teams, no winnerSolution A and B were built separately. On the same unseen matches, A won on dismissals, B on strike rate.→ Wrote the selection rule first, then ran the tournament.
"Why isn't Archer in?"RR's own strike bowler came out #45. Tempting to nudge him in.→ Stayed with the data; added a clearly labelled watchlist instead.
Dashboard ≠ reportA judge-facing chart showed Vaibhav at +76.9; the report said +48.7. Two pressure definitions had crept in.→ Unified on the report's definition; built a verifier: 10,172 checks, 0 failed.
THE EASY ANSWER VS WHAT WE SHIPPED
DecisionEasy answerShipped
Pressure definitionOvers 17–20 + required rate 9+ (the obvious rule)Win-probability leverage, validated (2.06× decisive share)
RatingRaw pressure strike rateContext-adjusted value, shrunk, + pressure SR, chosen on unseen matches
Best-looking versionA v3 (0.31 reliability)Rejected: it measured context
RR's own playersNudge Archer into the top 10Official list untouched; watchlist + RR review shown separately
Dashboard numbersTwo pressure definitions mixedGenerated from the pipeline and checked: 10,172 checks
Choosing the methodPick the version we liked bestPre-stated rule on 16 held-out cells: best worst case, then best mean
